title: Rigveda 9.37: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.37: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.37 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 681r-681v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.37.1-4 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 27); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 681r
translation.original_text:
1sa su̱taḥ pī̱taye̱ vṛṣā̱ soma̍ḥ pa̱vitre̍ arṣati | vi̱ghnan rakṣā̍ṁsi deva̱yuḥ ||
2sa pa̱vitre̍ vicakṣa̱ṇo hari̍r arṣati dharṇa̱siḥ | a̱bhi yoni̱ṁ kani̍kradat ||
3sa vā̱jī ro̍ca̱nā di̱vaḥ pava̍māno̱ vi dhā̍vati | ra̱kṣo̱hā vāra̍m a̱vyaya̍m ||
4sa tri̱tasyādhi̱ sāna̍vi̱ pava̍māno arocayat | jā̱mibhi̱ḥ sūrya̍ṁ sa̱ha ||
translation.text:
1SOMA, the Steer, effused for draught, flows to the purifying sieve, Slaying the fiends, loving the Gods.
2Far-sighted, tawny-coloured, he flows to the sieve, intelligent, Bellowing, to his place of rest.
3This vigorous Pavamâna runs forth to the luminous realm of heaven, Fiend-slayer, through the fleecy sieve.
4This Payamana up above Trita's high ridge hath made the Sun, Together with the Sisters, shine.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 681r (numbered 103r by the scribe) (OPenn image 681, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.36.1 ‹vājī ni akramīt›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 681v (numbered 103v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.37.5 ‹-asarat›. Verses 9.37.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1saḥ | sutaḥ | pītaye | vṛṣā | somaḥ | pavitre | arṣati | vi-ghnan | rakṣāṃsi | deva-yuḥ
2saḥ | pavitre | vi-cakṣaṇaḥ | hariḥ | arṣati | dharṇasiḥ | abhi | yonim | kanikradat
3saḥ | vājī | rocanā | divaḥ | pavamānaḥ | vi | dhāvati | rakṣaḥ-hā | vāram | avyayam
4saḥ | tritasya | adhi | sānavi | pavamānaḥ | arocayat | jāmi-bhiḥ | sūryam | saha

translation.original_ref: RV 9.37.5-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 27); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 681v
translation.original_text:
5sa vṛ̍tra̱hā vṛṣā̍ su̱to va̍rivo̱vid adā̍bhyaḥ | somo̱ vāja̍m ivāsarat ||
6sa de̱vaḥ ka̱vine̍ṣi̱to̱3̱̍ 'bhi droṇā̍ni dhāvati | indu̱r indrā̍ya ma̱ṁhanā̍ ||
translation.text:
5This Vr̥itra-slaying Steer, effused, Soma room-giver, ne'er deceived, Hath gone, as 'twere, to win the spoil.
6Urged onward by the sage, the God speeds forward to the casks of wood, Indu to Indra willingly.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 681v (numbered 103v by the scribe) (OPenn image 682, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.37.5 ‹-asarat›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 682r (numbered 104r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.39.3 ‹vi-rocayan›. Verses 9.37.5-6 end on this page; 9.37.5 begins on fol. 681r (numbered 103r by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
5saḥ | vṛtra-hā | vṛṣā | sutaḥ | varivaḥ-vit | adābhyaḥ | somaḥ | vājam-iva | asarat
6saḥ | devaḥ | kavinā | iṣitaḥ | abhi | droṇāni | dhāvati | induḥ | indrāya | maṃhanā
